description: A nine-panel composite TEM figure uniting bright-field TEM, HRTEM and IFFT-filtered images of dislocation–carbide interactions in samples fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa. (a,b) are bright-field TEM images (100 nm scale bars) showing intragranular κ-carbides (green arrows, labelled "Intragranular κ") and dislocation lines (blue arrows, labelled "Dislocation lines") in the fatigued 550-6 (a) and 650-6 (b) samples; in (b) the dislocation lines are denser and arrowed at four positions while three green circles mark carbides. (c,d) are HRTEM images (10 nm scale bars) of κ-carbides and dislocations in 550-6 (c) and 650-6 (d), each framed by a green rectangle. (c',d') are magnified views of those rectangles (5 nm scale bars), and (c'',d'') are the corresponding IFFT-filtered images (5 nm) in which κ-carbides, austenitic matrix and transition regions are delineated in white, black and blue respectively; red arrows in (c'',d'') point to localised contrast features. Together the panels argue that repeated dislocation shearing of nanosized intragranular κ-carbides under cyclic loading disrupts their ordered structure, forming shear steps and antiphase boundaries consistent with mechanical dissolution. No numeric values other than scale bars are printed.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (b) are bright-field TEM images carrying 100 nm scale bars, while (c) and (d) carry 10 nm scale bars and (c'), (c''), (d'), (d'') carry 5 nm scale bars.
Green arrows in (a) and green circles in (b) label 'Intragranular κ', and blue arrows in both panels label 'Dislocation lines'.
In (b) the dislocation lines appear denser and more closely spaced than in (a).
Panels (c') and (d') are magnified views of the green rectangular regions drawn in (c) and (d), respectively.
In the IFFT-filtered images (c'', d'') the κ-carbides, austenitic matrix and transition regions are highlighted in white, black and blue, respectively.
Red arrows in the IFFT panels mark shear steps and localised contrast variations within the carbides.
The figure concerns the fatigued 550-6 and 650-6 samples tested at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa.
The citing text states intragranular κ-carbides in 550-6 and 650-6 have average sizes of ~11 nm and ~24 nm, respectively, both remaining in the shearing regime.
The citing text reports a critical precipitate size of approximately 27 nm for the transition from shearing to Orowan bypassing in analogous alloy systems.

The citing text interprets the shear steps and localised contrast variations as disruption of the ordered structure and formation of antiphase boundaries, indicating mechanical dissolution of κ-carbides during cyclic loading.

In (d'') the κ-carbide regions delineated in white appear elongated/elliptical and larger than the corresponding white regions in (c''), consistent with the stated larger carbide size in the 650-6 sample.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM image of the fatigued 550-6 sample with a 100 nm scale bar; green arrows label 'Intragranular κ' and blue arrows label 'Dislocation lines' running through the matrix.
Bright-field TEM image of the fatigued 650-6 sample with a 100 nm scale bar; green circles mark 'Intragranular κ' particles and four blue arrows mark closely spaced 'Dislocation lines'.
HRTEM image (10 nm scale bar) of κ-carbides and dislocations in the fatigued 550-6 sample, with a green rectangle marking the region selected for magnification.
Magnified HRTEM view (5 nm scale bar) of the green rectangle in (c), showing lattice fringes of the carbide and surrounding matrix.

IFFT-filtered image (5 nm scale bar) corresponding to (c'); κ-carbides, austenitic matrix and transition regions are delineated in white, black and blue; two red arrows mark localised contrast features.
HRTEM image (10 nm scale bar) of κ-carbides and dislocations in the fatigued 650-6 sample, with a green rectangle marking the magnified region.
Magnified HRTEM view (5 nm scale bar) of the green rectangle in (d), showing carbide lattice fringes against a darker matrix.

IFFT-filtered image (5 nm scale bar) of (d'); elliptical/elongated κ-carbide regions are delineated in white with blue transition rims on a black austenitic matrix; two red arrows mark shear steps / contrast variations.
